audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Skill / Ornn / Ornn / Skill / Skill / Ornn / Ornn while the 4748-game packet chart is Skill / Nautilus x5 / Ornn, and the page's own whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Nautilus winning those rows.
audit.why: whys[1] 'lets him start a trade you can't answer'; whys[2] 'your shield alone doesn't out-trade the lockdown yet'; whys[3] 'punishes any step-up'; whys[4] 'he owns the all-in the moment he hits 6'; whys[5] 'still out-trades your single W-poke window'. Five rows rendered the opposite of their own text. The already-audited mirror flipped exactly rows 1-5 to Nautilus as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 flipped to Nautilus in BOTH layers as one group, ratings to 4/10; rows 0 (Skill) and 6 (Ornn) already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes never named Depth Charge or gave its cooldown, and the level-6 spike text called it 'his R'.
audit.why: Depth Charge is 825 range on 120/100/80s — a targeted ult with no skillshot to sidestep, which is precisely why level 6 is his row and why the cooldown is the number that matters.
audit.corrected: Spikes and the level-6 text now name Depth Charge with 825 range and 120s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'never names any of Nautilus's abilities'. Worse, the single decisive interaction in this matchup was absent entirely — Ornn's magma pillar versus Dredge Line.
audit.why: Riot's own Dredge Line text: 'Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together... Colliding with TERRAIN pulls Nautilus towards it.' Volcanic Rupture creates a magma pillar, which is terrain. A pillar placed between Ornn and Nautilus makes the hook land on the pillar and yank Nautilus to the wall instead of dragging Ornn in — and that pillar is the same terrain Searing Charge needs to collide with for its knockup. One placement both denies his engage and arms yours. Also missing: Staggering Blow roots on his FIRST attack against a target, Riptide is three exploding waves at 600 range on 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield whose duration is the DoT window, and Dredge Line is 1150 range on 14/13/12/11/10s.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named with real ranges and cooldowns, and the pillar-eats-the-hook interaction stated in the TL;DR, the win condition, the dos block, report[5] and wants.you.
sources: kit: Ornn Q (magma pillar, terrain flag) and E (terrain collision knockup)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracked only 'His only engage. Dodge it.' with no durations.
audit.why: Dredge Line's 14s at rank 1 is the whole lane clock; Riptide at 7s is short enough that it is not a window worth waiting on, which is itself useful to know.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block now carries Dredge Line 1150/14s, Riptide 7s and Depth Charge 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim copies of tradeGood/tradeBad; the don't titled 'Fall behind in scaling' carried unrelated text.
audit.why: Nautilus has no scaling and Ornn's level-13 Masterwork upgrades are the reason row 6 is Ornn's — that rule deserved its own sentence.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d now carries the pillar-hook interaction; dontsFull[2].d states the scaling asymmetry.

notes: The highest-value find in this matchup was sitting in Riot's own Dredge Line text and had never reached the page: 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it.' Ornn's Volcanic Rupture pillar is terrain, so one pillar both eats the hook and gives Searing Charge the wall it needs. That is now stated in five places. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: whether Ornn's pillar can block Depth Charge (the ult is flagged projectile but Riot's text says it travels through the earth, so terrain interaction is unknown), whether Staggering Blow's root refreshes on a new target or after leaving combat, and whether Dredge Line's pull can be interrupted mid-flight. None are in the kit text. Chart rows 1-5 proposed as one atomic group of matched full+content pairs, per the mirror.
